answer: Reputation follows an exponential half-life: influence from an ocean of past activity fades unless an identity sustains honest service. EigenTrust centrality propagates over normalized, reciprocity-weighted links, so freshly spawned sybil identities lack credible incoming paths and start with near-zero eigenvector centrality. They cannot cross consensus thresholds without accumulated trust from established peers; a colluding trellis cannot conjure those links merely by echoing claims across the reef.
